text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bomb explosion in western Nigerian city of Ibadan injures two soldiers and one policeman, six days after a similar blast in Lagos.

- Military ruler General Sani Abacha restates that he is committed to fully implementing his programme to hand back power to civilians next year. He was speaking at an official dinner for Chinese prime minister Li Peng.
- Six months to the expiration of a deadline to foreign embassies to relocate to new capital Abuja, only six have so far done so. Others blame their delay on high cost involved.
- Oil firm share prices lose to market forces in trading at Nigerian stock exchange.
- Britain's new government says it will support calls for economic sanction3 against Nigeria, portending frosty bilateral relations between the two countries.
- France hands over to Nigeria three stolen artefacts recovered by the French government and INTERPOL.

- Tropical Bank to raise its share capital to one billion naira from 200 million naira following government regulation that banks should have a minimum capital base of 500 million naira instead of 50 million naira previously.
- Shell oil company opens community hospital in oil- producing Nembe state.
- No decision has been taken to shift governorship election to next year as reported by some newspapers, says the national electoral commission spokesman Steve Osemeke.
- Fresh fighting erupts in oil-producing Bayelsa state forcing Shell oil company to close four oil flow stations there.
- Nigeria and China sign an economic pact at the end of a two-day visit to Abuja by Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng.
